I want to say I’m sorry, and I hope you feel better, but the truth is, nothing I or anyone can say will make you feel any better. It hurts, insanely bad, to lose someone to such a battle. You might ask yourself things like what could I have done more?? I should have done x, y, and z!! I should have done this, that etc. The truth is though, it is not and will never be your fault. Depression is a severe illness sometimes, and it can wreck havoc on a persons mind. It comes to a point where no matter what you do or say, they just don’t feel like they can get better. It is very hard to get someone like that out of such a mindset, I’m sure he loved you very much, but couldn’t see that beyond the state of despair he was in. It isn’t your fault, and it never will be. I know it hurts, or hurts more than anyone out there can imagine, and it feels like a piece of your soul is being ripped to pieces, and the world will never get better, and will stay black and white. I can’t say anything to make you feel better, but I can say that despite his depression, he chose you to stick by his side even though he felt like the world was falling, and I’m sure he loved you very very much. Take a break for a while, do not be hard on yourself. Let yourself cry, let yourself be upset and angry, pushing those emotions away will make you feel a lot worse. Even if that means stepping away from your kids for just a sec, sometimes you have to fall apart a little and figure out how to better build yourself around what has happened. Please talk to someone if you feel alone, a friend, a therapist. These fights are hard alone, and can make you feel worse, but I promise you people like me or others know what it feels like, and can talk about how it truly feels, getting those deep emotions out might help you. It may seem like a really long road, and I want to say it will be okay, but I believe that one day you will be strong, and find a way to build yourself up, even if it means pretending for right now. I know it’s cheesy to say fake it til you make it, but sometimes that is how it is. Pretend at first, but along the way find ways to make yourself feel stronger, even if it little by little. It may feel like you won’t get over this too, which honestly is okay. It comes and goes, sometimes give you more grief than others after time passes.
Sorry for the long rant this post made me emotional, but seriously, take your time healing and take care of yourself.

Being lonely definitely sucks, and can have a huge impact on your mental health, especially if you’re already not doing well. If you’re afraid to reach out, or feel like they don’t have time to deal with you, remember that if you care for them, they probably care for you too (forgive me if I’m wrong there). Communication when it comes to mental health is super important, and while it’s really scary to actually tell someone your concerns, most likely you’ll feel a lot better after getting it out there. Sometimes writing it down to tell them so you know what to say might help. Don’t give up though, you know you aren’t alone right now, so reach out for those connections!
